title: SurvUnc: A Meta-Model Based Uncertainty Quantification Framework for Survival Analysis

problem.claim: Survival analysis estimates event-occurrence probabilities over time from censored data and is important in high-stakes applications.

gap.claim: Uncertainty quantification for survival-model predictions remains underexplored and challenging, limiting model interpretability, trustworthiness, and adoption in sensitive applications.

contributions.claim: SurvUnc is a post-hoc, meta-model-based framework for uncertainty quantification in survival models.
SurvUnc uses anchor-based learning that integrates concordance knowledge and pairwise ranking performance into meta-model optimization for uncertainty estimation.
SurvUnc is model-agnostic and does not require survival-model architecture changes or access to internal parameters.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly introduce SurvUnc as a novel meta-model-based framework for post-hoc uncertainty quantification for survival models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a comprehensive evaluation pipeline for uncertainty quantification in survival analysis.

Across four publicly available benchmark datasets and five representative survival models, the authors report superiority across selective prediction, misprediction detection, and out-of-domain detection scenarios.
The authors report that SurvUnc enhances model interpretability and reliability and supports more trustworthy survival predictions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Survival analysis is used to estimate event-occurrence probabilities from censored data in high-stakes applications.
Prediction uncertainty is underexplored, challenging, and consequential for interpretability, trustworthiness, and adoption.
The paper introduces SurvUnc, combining post-hoc meta-modeling with anchor-based learning and concordance knowledge.
The framework is model-agnostic and is paired with a comprehensive evaluation pipeline.
Experiments on four datasets and five survival models report superiority across three evaluation scenarios and improved interpretability and reliability.

source_observation.claim: Uncertainty estimation can be added post hoc through a model-agnostic meta-model without modifying the underlying model or using its internal parameters.

interpretation.claim: A post-hoc, model-agnostic layer may reduce integration barriers for uncertainty quantification across heterogeneous survival models.

application.claim: Consider evaluating external uncertainty modules across multiple base models and downstream reliability tasks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported survival models, datasets, or evaluation scenarios.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baseline methods, quantitative results, or statistical significance.
The abstract does not describe implementation details, computational costs, or limitations.
